S3_Exploratory_Data_Analysis

Enrique Audain Martinez

2026-09-18

Exploratory Data Analysis

Brief description: Exploratory data analysis (EDA) is an approach to analyzing data sets to summarize their main characteristics, often with visual methods. A statistical model can be used or not, but primarily EDA is for seeing what the data can tell us beyond the formal modeling or hypothesis testing task.

0. Load the libraries

# Load the ggplot2 library
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)

1. Load the data

# Load the CHD gene annotation data
chd_genes <- read.delim("../../data/chd_genes.annotations.tsv", header = TRUE, sep = "\t")

# print the head of the data frame
head(chd_genes)
##   gene_symbol     category        pLI  plof gene_length obs_lof obs_syn exp_lof
## 1       ABCC9    syndromic 9.3524e-09 0.482      144002      30     298  84.399
## 2        ABL1    syndromic 9.9998e-01 0.176      173730       3     325  44.108
## 3       ACAD9    syndromic 4.5256e-08 0.814       36472      17     147  31.321
## 4       ACTA2 nonsyndromic 9.3017e-01 0.364       56317       2      72  17.293
## 5        ACTB    syndromic 9.8564e-01 0.232       36634       0     190  12.858
## 6       ACTC1 nonsyndromic 7.3668e-01 0.480        8044       2      89  13.125
##   exp_syn chromosome
## 1 298.160         12
## 2 314.370          9
## 3 144.410          3
## 4  84.674         10
## 5  96.859          7
## 6  89.788         15

2. Summarize the data

# Summarize the data

# Mean of the pLI score
mean(chd_genes$pLI) 
## [1] 0.4975205
# Median of the pLI score
median(chd_genes$pLI)
## [1] 0.5015
# Standard deviation of the pLI score
sd(chd_genes$pLI)
## [1] 0.4665019
# Maximum of the pLI score
max(chd_genes$pLI)
## [1] 1
# Minimum of the pLI score
min(chd_genes$pLI)
## [1] 1.5943e-68
# Summary of the pLI score
summary(chd_genes$pLI)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##  0.0000  0.0000  0.5015  0.4975  0.9991  1.0000

3. Visulization of the data using ggplot2

3.1 Histogram of gene length

Histogram: A histogram is an accurate representation of the distribution of numerical data.

# Histogram of gene length
ggplot(chd_genes, aes(x = gene_length)) + 
  geom_histogram() +
  labs(title = "Histogram of gene length", x = "Gene length", y = "Count")
## `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value with `binwidth`.

3.2 Boxplot of plof per category

Boxplot: A boxplot is a standardized way of displaying the distribution of data based on a five number summary: (minimum, first quartile (Q1), median, third quartile (Q3), and maximum).

# Boxplot per category
ggplot(chd_genes, aes(x = category, y = plof, fill=category)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Boxplot of plof per category", x = "category", y = "plof")

3.3 Scatter plot of obs_syn vs obs_lof

Scatter plot: A scatter plot (also called a scatterplot, scatter graph, scatter chart, scattergram, or scatter diagram) is a type of plot or mathematical diagram using Cartesian coordinates to display values for typically two variables.

# Scatter plot
ggplot(chd_genes, aes(x = obs_syn, y = obs_lof)) + 
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Scatter plot of obs_syn vs obs_lof")

3.4 Scatter plot with regression line and correlation coefficient

# Scatter plot with regression line and correlation coefficient
ggplot(chd_genes, aes(x = obs_syn, y = exp_syn)) + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Scatter plot with regression line") +
  stat_cor(method = "pearson", label.x = 100, label.y = 1500)
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

3.5 Density plot per category for plof metric

Density plot: A density plot is a smoothed, continuous version of a histogram estimated from the data.

# Density plot per category for plof metric
ggplot(chd_genes, aes(x = plof, fill = category)) + 
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Density plot")

3.6 Bar plot

# count number of genes per category
ggplot(chd_genes, aes(x = category, fill = category)) + 
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Bar plot of number of genes per category")

# count number of genes per chromosome
ggplot(chd_genes, aes(x = chromosome)) + 
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Bar plot of number of genes per chromosome")

# count number of genes per chromosome ordered (1,2,...,22,X,Y)
ggplot(chd_genes, aes(x = factor(chromosome, levels = c(1:22, "X", "Y")))) + 
  geom_bar() +
  ylab("Number of genes") +
  xlab("Chromosome") +
  labs(title = "Bar plot of number of genes per chromosome ordered")

4. Statistical tests

T-test: A t-test is a type of inferential statistic used to determine if there is a significant difference between the means of two groups, which may be related in certain features.

Wilcoxon test: The Wilcoxon test, which refers to either the Rank Sum test or the Signed Rank test, is a non-parametric test that compares two groups. It is the non-parametric equivalent of the t-test.

# t.test
t.test(pLI ~ category, data = chd_genes, alternative = "two.sided")
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  pLI by category
## t = -2.8937, df = 93.676, p-value = 0.004735
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group nonsyndromic and group syndromic is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -0.31798727 -0.05918087
## sample estimates:
## mean in group nonsyndromic    mean in group syndromic 
##                  0.3478832                  0.5364672
# wilcox.test
wilcox.test(pLI ~ category, data = chd_genes, alternative = "two.sided")
## 
##  Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction
## 
## data:  pLI by category
## W = 4390.5, p-value = 0.0005517
## alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0

5. Boxplot with statistical test

Note: A R-package can be extended to add new functionalities. The ggpubr package extends ggplot2 functionalities.

ggpubr::ggboxplot(chd_genes, 
          x = "category", 
          y = "plof",
          color = "category", 
          palette = "jco") +
  stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test", label.y = 2) +
  labs(title = "Boxplot of plof by category")

# Testing normality (U distribution)

u_dist = runif(1000, min = 2, max = 4)
shapiro.test(u_dist)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  u_dist
## W = 0.95571, p-value < 2.2e-16
hist(u_dist)

# Testing normality (N distribution)

n_dist = rnorm(1000, mean = 5, sd = 3)
shapiro.test(n_dist)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  n_dist
## W = 0.99775, p-value = 0.1938
hist(n_dist)

shapiro.test(chd_genes$plof)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  chd_genes$plof
## W = 0.92043, p-value = 5.789e-11
